title: Credit Administration Standard for Farm Real Estate Loans: Applications, Collateral Limits and Closing Conditions
content:
**Product:** Farm Real Estate Loans (all FarmLand products)

## 1. Application and credit decision

1.1 An application is registered with the product's official name, the amount and the installment frequency, and a credit officer decides it; the servicing desk never approves or declines.

## 2. Amount and collateral

2.1 The amount must lie between the product's smallest original principal and its largest original principal.

2.2 The amount may not exceed the value-weighted average of the product's largest loan-to-value by land use over the parcels to be mortgaged, applied to their appraised value.

2.3 An amount above the product's appraisal threshold needs a full appraisal; any other amount needs an evaluation.

2.4 A parcel that secures a Country Home loan in active status cannot also be mortgaged to a farm real estate loan. This is judged on the system record of the Rural Home Loans side — the Country Home loan's property parcel number and its status — checked before the parcel is mortgaged, and it is matched to the parcel being mortgaged by its county parcel number; a member's statement does not replace that record.

## 3. Term

3.1 The amortization may not exceed the product's longest amortization, and the frequency must be one of the product's installment frequencies allowed.

3.2 A rate quoted at application is held for the product's rate-lock days, counted in calendar days from the lock date; a loan closing later takes the rate of the current sheet.

## 4. Conditions of closing

The loan closes only when all three of the following hold:

- the member holds the stock required under the Member Equities & Patronage borrower stock requirement;
- hazard insurance names the association mortgagee where insurable buildings exceed the product's buildings insurance threshold;
- flood insurance is in force on buildings in a special flood hazard area.

## 5. Origination fee

5.1 On closing, an origination fee of the product's origination fee percentage of the original principal, bounded by the product's minimum and maximum origination fee, is assessed. The percentage of the original principal is rounded to cents first; that amount is raised to the minimum fee if it is lower, and then held to the maximum fee if it is higher.

## Points of judgement

| Situation | Result under this standard |
|---|---|
| Amount below the product's smallest original principal, or above its largest | outside the amount bounds |
| Amount exactly at the appraisal threshold | an evaluation |
| Amount above the appraisal threshold | a full appraisal |
| Parcel to be mortgaged is the property parcel of a Country Home loan in active status | cannot be mortgaged to the farm real estate loan |
| Requested frequency not in the product's allowed list | not available on that product |
| Closing after the rate-lock period | rate of the current sheet |

**Origination fee illustration (hypothetical).** An original principal of USD 1234567.89 on a product with a 0.5 percent fee, a USD 500 minimum and a USD 7500 maximum: 0.5 percent is USD 6172.84 after rounding to cents, which is above the minimum and below the maximum, so the fee is USD 6172.84.
